title: Root canal treatment
what: The dentist removes the inflamed nerve from inside the tooth, cleans the canals in the roots, and seals them tightly. The tooth is saved.
why: For an inflamed tooth nerve, a dead nerve, or infection at the tip of the root. Sometimes before a crown.
duration: usually 1 to 2 hours per visit, often 1 to 3 visits
tell_doctor: Heart disease, artificial heart valves, or diabetes
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
If the tooth has been treated before

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat 1 to 2 hours before your visit. The visit is long, and eating is hard while you are numb.

prepare.title: Pain
prepare.text: If the tooth hurts, you can take your usual painkiller. Tell the dentist what you took and when.

bring: X-rays of the tooth, if you have them
steps: The dentist takes an X-ray to see the roots and canals
The tooth is isolated with a thin rubber sheet, so no saliva gets into the canals
Through a small opening in the tooth, the nerve is removed and the canals are cleaned with fine tools
The canals are rinsed with a medicated solution
The canals are filled right away, or medicine and a temporary filling are put in until the next visit
At the end, a check X-ray is taken
feel: While numb: pressure and vibration, but no pain
Keeping your mouth open for a long time is tiring. You can ask for a break
after: For a few days, the tooth may ache when you bite. This is usual
Take a painkiller if needed. The dentist will tell you which one
Do not chew on that side while you have a temporary filling
After a root canal, the tooth often needs a strong filling or a crown. Otherwise it may crack
Go to all your visits. Unfinished treatment can end with losing the tooth
red_flags: Swelling of the cheek, gum, or under the eye that keeps getting worse
Trouble swallowing, breathing, or opening your mouth: call emergency services right away

faq.a: With modern numbing, usually not. You feel pressure. After treatment, the tooth may ache for a few days.

faq.q: Why does a root canal take several visits?
faq.a: If there is strong inflammation, medicine is left in the canals for a while. When it calms down, the canals are sealed.

faq.q: Why do I need a crown after a root canal?
faq.a: Without its nerve, a tooth becomes more fragile. A crown or a strong filling protects it from cracks.
